transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-01 16:00 PDT
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Product); Priya Nair (CobaltCare), Ethan Brooks (SRE), Jin Park (Security), Samir Patel (ML)

Summary:
Quick technical workshop to walk through request-level diagnostics in the Console, how to triage OOMs / tokencount spikes, and designing a failover playbook for private/dedicated fallback. Customer wants to understand traces, request logs, and how to automate fallback to cheaper model variants without losing SLA.

Topics covered:
- Request trace navigation and correlation IDs
- KV cache miss patterns and debugging for long-context prompts
- Error classification (OOM, timeout, model mismatch) and recommended remediation steps
- Failover orchestration: canary -> warm standby -> polyfill model options
- Security considerations for VPC/private deployments and audit logs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: okay everyone, thanks for jumping on. I'm Maya from Redwood, i'll kick off, Diego will drive the deep trace demos, lena might chime for product notes. Priya, wanna give a quick bit of context on what you're seeing?
[00:12] Priya: yeah thanks, uh we've been seeing intermittent latency and some dropped requests during peak, um mostly on our summarization route. Some requests come back with truncated output or 5xxs, sometimes it's OOMs we think. We're running a mixed workload, long-doc summaries and short chat queries.
[00:28] Diego: got it. quick question, are you on Dedicated or hosted?
[00:31] Priya: Dedicated right now, committed pool but we've bumped usage last month, so there were bursts.
[00:36] Maya: perfect. so today's plan: show you Console traces, how to map request ids to model runtimes, look at KV cache histograms, and then we sketch a failover playbook that preserves latency SLOs.
[00:48] Ethan: and also we want to know how our logs get out — like retention, who can see them, and where the PII scrubbing happens.
[00:55] Jin: yes security concerns are top, HIPAA plus our supplier rules.
[01:00] Diego: noted. i'll start with a live trace. bear with me, audio is a bit choppy, i might mispronounce things — the UI shows a request timeline, the left shows span waterfall, top right is model metadata and exec metrics, bottom is raw request/response. here's an example id — 8f7b-duplicated-trans — sorry the transcriber sometimes munges ids.
[01:22] [screen share noises]
[01:26] Diego: so this request shows a long KV-cache build up, you can see repeated cache misses at t=0.4s, 0.8s, that's typically from varying prompt prefixes. In your logs we saw similar pattern.
[01:38] Samir: are the misses tied to conversation id or to prompt tokenization?
[01:41] Diego: good question. usually it's prompt prefix variability; tokenizer diffs cause different cache keys. Our suggestion: normalize the prefix or use stable prompt templates. Also we surfaced a 'kv-hit-rate' field in the trace. yours is like 36% in the bad run.
[01:57] Priya: 36% that low? okay. what's a good target?
[02:01] Diego: 70%+ for long-doc summaries. under 50% you start incurring more token compute and OOM risk.
[02:09] Ethan: and that ties to cost spikes too right?
[02:12] Maya: yes, low cache hits -> more decoder steps -> more GPU time -> cost + latency. Optimize will suggest batching and quantization but we can discuss that separately.
[02:23] [brief crosstalk]
[02:30] Diego: moving on, here's a 5xx trace. span shows 'model-error: OOM' with GPU mem peak 95%. There's an inner restart span where the request retried on a lower context model variant. The console marks that as a fallback.
[02:45] Priya: wait, is restart automatic or configured?
[02:48] Diego: it can be both. by default you get a simple automatic retry to same model for transient infra failures; but you can configure policy: on OOM -> retry with smaller context model (e.g., gpt-large-16k -> gpt-medium-8k) or enable a polyfill model.
[02:59] Samir: how do you ensure semantic fidelity with smaller model? we can't afford hallucinations on clinical notes.
[03:03] Lena: that's where canary and rollouts come in, plus Eval sets. you define quality thresholds; if polyfill drops below threshold, don't route user traffic. Also Redwood Optimize can simulate expected quality loss.
[03:15] Jin: can we get an audit log for every automatic fallback decision? we need traceability.
[03:20] Diego: yes, Console emits a 'fallback_reason' field and a unique decision id. All decisions are logged in audit trail; you can filter by user, route, or decision id.
[03:28] Jin: good. need that for compliance.
[03:30] [00:03:45 marker glitch]
[03:34] Diego: i want to show the request logs panel now — you can search by correlation id, user id, or model shard. note the search supports wildcard and time-range. here's the raw payload view, you'll see prompt, token counts, and the KV cache snapshot (trimmed). sometimes the tokenizer name is wrong in the transcript — it's 'tiktoken' but console shows the tokenizer used.
[03:55] Ethan: speaking of token counts, we noticed sudden jumps to 20k tokens on some requests; is console able to flag anomalous token spikes?
[04:03] Diego: yes there's an anomaly detector that surfaces outliers. you can configure thresholds per-route. we also tag requests with 'suspect_long_prefix' and surface suggested remediation like 'trim system prompt' or 'divide document'.
[04:16] Priya: okay that's useful. can it auto-split a long doc into chunks and reassemble?
[04:21] Maya: Redwood doesn't rewrite your app, but Optimize has a chunking helper and SDK primitives to recombine with minimal coherence loss. we can share a sample transform.
[04:32] [long pause, typing]
[04:40] Diego: next i want to talk about correlation between infra metrics and request errors. the console ties GPU utilization, queue length, and per-model tail-latency with request traces. in your case we saw queue spikes preceding 5xx bursts, likely autoscaler lag.
[04:55] Ethan: autoscaler lag? we're on reserved capacity with autoscale. do you recommend adjusting thresholds?
[04:59] Diego: usually reduce cooldown and pre-warm policy. also configure burst capacity for business-critical routes. we can show recommended autoscale profiles.
[05:07] Priya: any cost implications?
[05:09] Maya: small increases in reserved peak can massively cut 5xx risk; Optimize will show cost delta.
[05:14] Samir: on the security angle, where do logs live in private deploy? we need them inside the VPC and to use our KMS.
[05:20] Lena: in Private deployments logs can be routed to customer-managed storage and you can integrate with your KMS/HSM for encryption. audit logs remain available in the Console but only over private control plane.
[05:31] Jin: can we get a diagram of what data leaves our VPC?
[05:34] Maya: yes, i'll attach a network flow diagram and the security brief.
[05:38] Diego: back to failover playbook. step 1 classify error: transient infra vs model semantic failure. step 2 map remediation: transient -> retry/backoff or route to warm standby; OOM -> reduce context or polyfill; semantic fail -> flag for manual review and revert rollout. here's a sample playbook flow in the UI.
[05:57] Priya: we need automated alerts to oncall with context. can alerts include links to the exact trace?
[06:02] Diego: yes every alert includes trace link, decision id, and pre-populated runbook steps.
[06:07] Ethan: what about replaying a request to debug? we sometimes want to re-run a failed request in a sandbox.
[06:12] Diego: Console supports request replays to a sandbox model; you can replay at varying model configs and inspect diffs. note: replay uses scrubbed payload by default if PII is detected.
[06:23] Jin: how good is the PII detection? it's not perfect, right?
[06:26] Lena: it's heuristic plus customer rules; you can add suppression regex, or send data to your scrubbing service before storing.
[06:33] Priya: let's talk RTO and RPO expectations for failover — we need an SLA estimate.
[06:38] Maya: for Dedicated with warm standby and autoscale tuned, typical RTO is under 30s for routing decisions, full model spin-up depends on instance pool. we'll provide numbers per config.
[06:49] Samir: curious about KV cache behavior when failing over to a smaller model — do you preserve cache or rebuild?
[06:54] Diego: the cache keys are model-architecture specific. a fallback to smaller model usually has separate cache; we do best-effort semantic approximation but it's not identical. recommended approach: maintain lightweight prefix-only cache to preserve some locality.
[07:07] [pause]
[07:10] Priya: one more thing: we have a legal review next week, we need a one-pager showing auditability and fallback controls.
[07:16] Maya: we'll provide a one-pager and attach the security packet.
[07:19] [screen share: failover playbook image]
[07:25] Diego: i'm going to demo a synthetic repro: sending repeated 12k token requests to stress the KV and show the console marking degradations. if it fails the first model, you'll see automatic routing to polyfill.
[07:38] [keyboard clatter, micro pause]
[07:44] Diego: okay triggered. trace shows mem climb, OOM, retry span, fallback model selected. note in console we flagged 'quality_estimate: 0.93' for the polyfill in this synthetic case — in your workloads you'll want a dedicated eval set.
[07:59] Priya: that quality number — where does it come from? is it historical eval or on-the-fly?
[08:03] Diego: from historical evals and latest rollout metrics; the console updates as you collect more production signals.
[08:09] Ethan: about instrumentation — do we need any SDK changes to get full traces?
[08:12] Diego: minimal. we recommend adding the Redwood request-id header and sending user-id if you want correlation. SDKs auto-instrument token counts and user meta if present.
[08:21] Samir: can we redact user ids in traces but keep correlation? some teams need pseudonymous tracing.
[08:24] Lena: yep; pseudonymization is supported — we replace PII with reversible tokens under your KMS.
[08:30] Jin: okay actionable ask: send the failover runbook, security packet, and sample replay SOP.
[08:35] Maya: noted, will send.
[08:38] [closing recap]
[08:40] Maya: recap — Diego will run KV repro and share results; Maya to send docs and pricing; Priya team to share example request ids and security constraints. schedule pilot after logs posted. any objections?
[08:51] Priya: none. good session. thanks.
[08:54] Ethan: thanks everyone.
[08:56] [meeting end]
